title: Choose a placement grid without changing footprint geometry
summary: Use a documented placement grid and origin for orderly alignment. A 0.25 mm grid is an optional project choice; use finer or local grids for constrained placement and snap routing to actual pads.
applies_to: PCB placement; not a schematic connectivity grid.
required_inputs: Footprint pitch, mechanical datums and routing density
verification: Check component coordinates and actual pad connectivity after placement.
limitations: Never distort footprint pad pitch or move mechanically fixed parts to satisfy a cosmetic grid.

citations.locator: Imperial or Metric Grid; Defining the Purpose of a Grid; object hotspot snapping

title: Group circuits by function while preserving return paths
summary: Keep related circuits together and separate noisy switching paths from sensitive inputs. Plan inter-block signals and returns before routing.
required_inputs: Functional blocks, noise sources and sensitive receivers
verification: Review current loops and reference continuity at every block crossing.
limitations: Functional partitioning does not require cutting the ground plane; symmetry does not override electrical placement.

citations.locator: Practical PCB Design Rules, pages 10-12, Figures 7-10

title: Set signal spacing from coupling and timing requirements
summary: Fabrication clearance is not a signal-integrity target. Review aggressor edge rate, parallel length, separation and distance to the reference plane; increase spacing or change the route where coupling exceeds the victim noise budget.
applies_to: Adjacent signal routes, especially switching signals near analog sense lines.
required_inputs: Stackup, edge rates, parallel lengths and receiver noise margin
verification: Model or measure coupled noise at the victim under worst intended switching activity.
limitations: No universal 3W rule guarantees acceptable coupling. Preserve the specified geometry inside a differential pair.

citations.locator: Discussion of Figures 2-4: coupling, spacing and reference-plane distance

title: Review pad entry and narrow copper features
summary: Use pad snapping to form a deliberate connection; centered entry is a useful default, not a universal requirement. Inspect narrow copper necks, slivers and gaps against the fabrication rules.
applies_to: Trace-to-pad connections and dense copper geometry.
required_inputs: Pad geometry, trace width and fabricator feature limits
verification: Run connectivity and clearance checks on final copper, then inspect manufacturing output.
limitations: Do not infer etching failure from an angle alone or force a detour solely to reach a pad center. Special breakout and Kelvin geometries require their own review.

title: Use teardrops where connection robustness benefits
summary: Consider teardrops at vulnerable trace-to-pad, via and neck-down junctions, particularly where drill misregistration or flex stress can weaken a connection.
applies_to: Fabrication and mechanical robustness of copper junctions.
required_inputs: Drill tolerances, junction geometry and assembly process
verification: Repour and rerun clearance checks after generation; inspect the final copper and any controlled-impedance transition.
limitations: Teardrops are optional and do not replace annular-ring rules or qualify a flex design. Dense pads may leave insufficient room.

title: Define enclosure fit and manufacturable outline geometry
summary: Define the outline, holes and cutouts from mechanical datums and tolerances. Account for the milling tool radius at internal corners before checking enclosure fit.
applies_to: Routed rigid PCB outlines and cutouts.
required_inputs: Enclosure drawing, tolerances, mounting points and milling capability
verification: Compare the closed outline and hole positions with mechanical CAD and the fabrication drawing.
limitations: External rounding and visual symmetry are choices, not universal manufacturing requirements. Eurocircuits describes a 2 mm tool giving 1 mm internal radius; confirm the selected service.

citations.locator: PCB Contour; Internal Corners; Cut-outs and Slots

title: Place connectors from mating geometry and enclosure access
summary: Place external connectors using the selected part drawing and enclosure opening. Check mating travel, overhang, retention and service access rather than measuring from silkscreen text.
applies_to: External connector placement; USB4105 is one device-specific example.
required_inputs: Connector drawing, board-edge datum, enclosure and mating plug envelope
verification: Check the assembled mechanical envelope and demonstrate insertion and removal.
limitations: Not every connector belongs on the perimeter; internal board-to-board connectors may require interior placement. Do not transfer USB4105 dimensions to another part.

citations.locator: Recommended PCB layout and mating views

title: Evaluate a stitched edge guard rather than a lone perimeter trace
summary: Where edge radiation is relevant, evaluate ground copper tied to the appropriate reference planes with a via fence. A perimeter trace alone does not form the multilayer shielding structure.
applies_to: Multilayer edge-radiation review; ADI evidence is from iCoupler evaluation boards.
required_inputs: Stackup, relevant frequencies, ground domains and copper-to-edge limits
verification: Check every fence connection and isolation keepout; measure emissions and supply noise after layout changes.
limitations: ADI notes that reflected energy can increase plane noise. Its 4 mm evaluation-board via pitch is not a universal rule or compliance guarantee. Never bridge an isolation barrier with ground copper.

citations.locator: Edge Guarding, Figures 9-10; Interplane Capacitance fill discussion

title: Keep legend clear of exposed copper and openings
summary: Keep silkscreen clear of solderable pads, exposed copper, holes and cutouts using the manufacturing and assembly clipping rules. Copper covered by soldermask is not itself a silkscreen exclusion.
applies_to: Legend clearance review on soldermasked PCBs.
required_inputs: Final soldermask openings, via treatment and assembler clipping rules
verification: Inspect the production legend after clipping; confirm that required labels remain intact.
limitations: Do not rely on tentative via tenting to preserve a label. Printing over a suitably masked filled/capped via is process-dependent; an open hole remains unsuitable.

citations.locator: Design Rules; Minimum Clearances; Legend Clipping

title: Choose legible text geometry for the ordered process
summary: Check rendered stroke width, character height, spacing and orientation against the fabricator limits. A 1.5-2 mm text height can be a project readability preference, not a universal minimum.
applies_to: PCB legend labels and service markings.
required_inputs: Fabricator legend limits and final label geometry
verification: Review final-size output and production clipping, including fine gaps in inverted text.
limitations: No particular font is required. Eurocircuits lists 1.0 mm text height and 0.10 mm strokes; these are service-specific, not portable defaults.

citations.locator: Text and Line Specifications; Approving the Legend Clipping

title: Make pin one and polarity unambiguous
summary: Provide unambiguous pin-one or orientation markings consistent with the exact component datasheet. Verify polarized components and connectors against their footprint numbering and assembly data.
applies_to: Polarized and orientation-sensitive SMD and through-hole components.
required_inputs: Component datasheet, footprint mapping and assembly orientation
verification: Compare markings with the assembled view and ensure essential indicators survive clipping.
limitations: A square pad or generic dot alone does not establish cathode, positive terminal or ground. If pin one is not defined, use an explicit orientation cue.

citations.locator: Orientation of Surface Mount Components; Orientation of Through Hole Components

title: Check mask color against process capability and inspection needs
summary: Choose mask color after checking the ordered process, mask bridges, legend visibility, price and lead time. Color is not evidence of electrical quality.
required_inputs: Copper weight, pad spacing and current fabrication capabilities
verification: Confirm the selected color and finish together in the quote and DFM review.
limitations: Do not assume every color has identical fine-pitch capability or cost. Capability tables may distinguish black/white from other masks; use the current service limits.
